STEP 1 - Scene: A small portion of cooked meat (appears to be steak or similar beef, medium-rare, with a bit of red sauce or juices) on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-overhead angle. Only one small piece of food is on the plate.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 26 cm across. Vessel area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2 (for a square plate, roughly 26 x 26 = 676 cm^2 gross, but the rounded corners make the usable area closer to 530 cm^2; I use 530 cm^2).

STEP 3 - Items: One cooked beef steak portion, sliced, with a small amount of red sauce/juices.

STEP 4 - Area: The meat strip covers about 60 cm^2, roughly 11% of the plate area.

STEP 5 - Volume: The strip is about 10 cm long, 2.5 cm wide and 1 cm thick at its thickest, giving an outer envelope of about 60 cm^2 x 1 cm ≈ 60 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: 60 ml x 0.95 g/ml ≈ 57 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked beef steak ≈ 250 kcal/100 g (medium, lean-to-fatty cut). 57 g x 2.5 = about 143 kcal. Sauce residue is minor (~3 g at ~100 kcal/100 g ≈ 3 kcal), so the total is roughly 146 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A single thin steak strip of about 57 g is plausible for what is visible, and it is far below a full dinner plate, which fits the small amount of food shown.
